title: Speak and respond in everyday situations in X

lessons.title: Speaking clearly at work
lessons.html:
Speaking clearly at work

Every day at work you speak to people: your team, your supervisor, clients, suppliers and visitors. This unit is about speaking and responding well in everyday situations in your chosen language (X). Good speaking builds trust, prevents mistakes and helps you get things done.

Everyday speaking situations

  • Greeting people and introducing yourself.
  • Giving and receiving instructions.
  • Asking questions and asking for help.
  • Reporting a problem to your supervisor.
  • Talking to a client about their garden.
  • Using the phone or a two-way radio.
  • Taking part in a team meeting.

Tips for clear speaking

  • Face the person and make eye contact, if that is respectful in your culture and theirs.
  • Speak at a steady speed, not too fast.
  • Speak loudly enough, but do not shout.
  • Use words the listener knows. Explain work words if needed.
  • Give one instruction at a time.
  • Use polite words: please, thank you, excuse me, sorry.

Greeting and respect

In South Africa there are many cultures and languages. Greet people properly. Use titles like Mr, Mrs, Ma'am, Sir, or respectful forms like Baba and Mama where suitable. Learn a greeting in the languages of your co-workers. It shows respect.

Example: reporting a problem

Thabo: Good morning, Mrs Naidoo. Sorry to interrupt. The brush cutter will not start. I checked the fuel and it is full. Can I take the other one from the store, or should I wait for the mechanic?

Thabo greets, says sorry for interrupting, explains the problem, says what he already checked, and asks a clear question.

lessons.title: Listening and responding
lessons.html:
Listening and responding

Speaking is only half of the conversation. You must also listen and respond.

Active listening

  • Stop what you are doing and look at the speaker.
  • Do not interrupt.
  • Nod or say yes, I see, to show you are listening.
  • Ask a question if something is not clear.
  • Repeat the main point back: So you want the hedges cut before Friday?

Receiving instructions

  1. Listen to the whole instruction.
  2. Ask about anything you do not understand: which bed, how many, by when?
  3. Repeat it back in your own words.
  4. If you cannot do it, say so and explain why, for example you do not have the right tool or you are not trained.

Talking to clients

  • Greet them and say who you are and who you work for.
  • Listen to what they want. Ask questions.
  • Do not promise things you are not allowed to promise, like prices. Say: I will ask my supervisor and we will come back to you.
  • Stay polite even if the client is unhappy. Call your supervisor if needed.

Using the phone or radio

  • Say your name and where you are.
  • Keep it short and clear.
  • On a radio, say over when you finish speaking and wait for the reply.
  • Write down important information, like a time or address.

Body language and tone

How you say something is as important as what you say. Folded arms, rolling eyes or an angry tone can upset people even if your words are polite. Keep a calm voice and open body.

Taking part in meetings

  • Wait your turn to speak.
  • Give your ideas clearly and briefly.
  • Disagree politely: I see your point, but I think...

Key points

  • Speak clearly, at a steady speed, with polite words.
  • Greet people with respect.
  • Listen actively and repeat the main point back.
  • Ask questions when an instruction is not clear.
  • Do not promise clients things you are not allowed to promise.
